per_trial_seed_pattern.context: Inside _standard_trial_loop, called once per trial. seed comes from session.get("seed", 42), trial in 0..99.

item_3_generation_seed_audit.temperature_in_seed_offset_explanation: CRITICAL: the seed offset is "seed + trial" with NO temperature in the formula. The seed for (Q0039, trial=27, T=0.0) equals the seed for (Q0039, trial=27, T=0.2) equals ... equals (Q0039, trial=27, T=1.0) = 42 + 27 = 69. Each temperature loop reuses the same RNG sequence per trial.

do_sample_handling.note: Generation correctly switches to do_sample=True for T>0. So T>0 IS sampling; the question is whether the same RNG sequence at different temperatures should produce different outputs.

item_3_generation_seed_audit.expected_behavior_under_correct_collecti: With do_sample=True and same RNG seed, different temperatures should produce DIFFERENT outputs because temperature rescales the logit distribution before sampling. The same uniform draw from RNG state lands on different tokens under different temperature scalings of the logit softmax. So duplicate md5 across T=0.2..T=1.0 is NOT explainable by "same seed, same code path" -- it indicates either (a) generation pulled from a non-sampling path despite do_sample=True, (b) hidden states from one run were copied over others, or (c) the apparatus computed generation once and reused across all temperatures.
